info.desc: 52nd Street is the sixth studio album by American singer-songwriter Billy Joel, released on October 13, 1978. It was the first of four Joel albums to top the Billboard charts and earned him two Grammys (for a total of four). It was also the first ever music CD to be commercialized. Three songs reached the Top 40 in the United States, contributing to the album's success: "My Life" (#3), "Big Shot" (#14), and "Honesty" (#24). It was similarly well received by critics, earning the 1979 Grammy for Album of the Year. This Grammy was presented to its producer, Phil Ramone. .

podcast.body: According to legend, "52nd Street" was the first of 50 titles simultaneously issued by Sony Japan on October 1, 1982, marking a significant early release in the format's history. "On October 1, 1982, Sony Japan issued 50 titles all at once. And according to legend, the first of those 50 was 52nd Street from Billy Joel."

podcast.body: Billy Joel's album "52nd Street" went on sale in Japan in October 1982, and it might have been one of the very first commercially available Compact Discs to hit the market. However, there is ongoing dispute regarding the definitive first commercially released CD. "Maybe it's Billy Joel's 52nd Street."

podcast.body: Billy Joel's album *52nd Street* was the first album to be released on CD as a reissue. This historic release signaled the beginning of artists' existing catalogs being transferred to the new digital format. "The first album to be released on CD was a reissue of Billy Joel's 52nd Street."

podcast.body: This album was reissued in 1983 and became the first Compact Disc manufactured in the United States. Its release was an important milestone for the CD's penetration into the American market, following its earlier commercial introduction. "en 1983 tuvimos el primero hecho en los Estados Unidos, que fue una redición de Billio El."

When the first 50 CD titles were released in Japan on October 1, 1982, Billy Joel's `52nd Street` was at the very top of that list, determined by the sequence of catalog numbers. This indicates its prominence in the initial rollout of the compact disk format. `"And if we go by the sequence of catalog numbers, the CD at the top of that list was Billy Joel's 52nd Street."`
